title: And Are We Wretches Yet Alive
description: And Are We Wretches Yet Alive in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 105, headed “Repentance flowing from the patience of God”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And are we wretch-es yet a-live? And do we yet re-bel? 'Tis bound-less, 'tis a-ma-zing love That bears us up from hell!

lines: And are we wretches yet alive?
That bears us up from hell!
The burden of our weighty guilt
Would sink us down to flames,
And dare we now provoke his wrath,
Lord, we have long abus'd thy love,
Our aching hearts e'en bleed to see
No more, ye lusts, shall ye command,
Stretch out, O God, thy conquering hand,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
